answer: Adult skin fibroblasts express high levels of inflammatory markers (IL6, IL1RA), antigen presentation genes (HLA-A), innate immune and inflammatory response genes (CD55, PTGES), and cellular senescence genes (CDKN1A). In contrast, prenatal skin fibroblasts upregulate genes involved in immune suppression (CD200), regulation of inflammation (RAMP2), and tissue regeneration (MDK). Additionally, prenatal fibroblasts do not significantly express papillary fibroblast markers such as COL13A1.
support_quote: All adult fibroblast subsets expressed high levels of inflammatory cytokines and receptors (for example, IL6 and IL1RA) and genes involved in antigen presentation (for example, HLA-A), innate immune and inflammatory responses (for example, CD55 and PTGES) and cellular senescence (CDKN1A). By contrast, prenatal skin fibroblasts had upregulated genes involved in immune suppression (CD200), regulation of inflammation (for example, RAMP2) and tissue regeneration (MDK).
